messages:
carol-support: incoming support escalation — Erin Corp reports sustained TLS handshake tail for API calls from eu-west (p95 ~320ms -> p95 baseline ~75ms, p99 up to 780ms). They provided a sample request id: req_0a7c8.
carol-support: attaching quick probe:
carol-support: dig +short api.redwood.example @8.8.8.8 -> 34.101.12.45
carol-support: curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect}\n time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example -> time_connect:0.120 time_appconnect:0.680
alice-net: thanks. which eu-west pop and customer ASN?
carol-support: customer source ASN 3320, seen from eu-west-1 (zone eu-west-3 probe). ticket includes a traceroute snippet.
bob-sre: kicked off active probes from multiple eu probes. initial MTR shows an extra ~160ms hop between eu-pop-03 and transit-ix for certain paths, consistent with hairpin to us backbone. Also seeing two different anycast answers on DNS during spikes (fast switch between A records).
alice-net: can you paste the traceroute sample?
bob-sre: traceroute excerpt:
 1  10.0.3.1 (10.0.3.1)  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 6  transit-ix-12.example.net  12.1 ms  13.2 ms  12.8 ms
 7  us-backbone-gw.example.net  172.5 ms  171.9 ms  173.0 ms
 8  api-redwood-eu.example.net  173.6 ms  174.1 ms  173.2 ms
bob-sre: note the sudden jump at hop 7 -> indicates cross-region handoff for subset of flow. also tcpdump at edge shows complete TLS client hello issued but server SNI handshake delayed until different anycast IP answered.
dave-ops: who pushed routing/GSLB changes overnight? I see a controlled weight rebalance at 02:10 UTC to drain eu-pop-03 for infra work (change id rb-2024-11-07-0210).
alice-net: that matches — weight shift triggered some clients to be routed via fallback path which uses a US peering path for those ASNs, adding ~150ms. Also DNS TTL was low (30s) so flapping caused some packets to re-resolve mid-flow.
dave-ops: mitigation plan: rollback the weight change to restore eu-pop preference, increase GSLB stabilize window from 30s to 300s for eu regions, and raise dns TTL for api endpoint to 120s while we validate. approve?
bob-sre: +1. also add a short-term route pin for customer ASN 3320 to prefer eu-pop-03 (sticky policy) until we complete postmortem.
carol-support: notified customer of mitigations and asked them to stay on a sample test for 15 min.
deploy-bot: rollback executed: action rb-2024-11-07-0210 -> reverted at 03:02 UTC by dave-ops (CI run id: ci-9823).
bob-sre: re-ran probes after rollback: p95 dropped to 88ms (from 320ms), p99 to 150ms (from 780ms). tcpdump shows consistent anycast answer now.
erin-cust: thanks, we're seeing normal latency again on our side. Will monitor over next hour. :thumbsup:
carol-support: marking as mitigated for now. next steps: 1) postmortem on GSLB rollout policy + canary ramping; 2) update runbook to include sticky routing for critical ASNs; 3) add an automated probe that compares path hop counts for eu origin traffic and alerts on cross-region handoff.
alice-net: also recommend adding a preflight check in rollout that simulates DNS churn for low-ttl endpoints and measures p95 impact before full weight change.
dave-ops: agreed. I'll open follow-up ticket and schedule a change to increase default GSLB stabilization window.
carol-support: logging ticket id PM-4821 and will follow up with Erin Corp. leaving this thread open for 72h observation but closing escalation.
carol-support: note for SRE/infra: correlate any future TLS tail regressions with recent GSLB or peering changes as first triage step.
